Bug_Title: Double-checked locking should not be used
Bug_Details:
Double-checked locking is the practice of checking a lazy-initialized object’s state both before and after a synchronized block is
entered to determine whether to initialize the object. In early JVM versions, synchronizing entire methods was not performant, which sometimes caused
this practice to be used in its place.
Apart from float and int types, this practice does not work reliably in a platform-independent manner without additional
synchronization of mutable instances. Using double-checked locking for the lazy initialization of any other type of primitive or mutable object risks
a second thread using an uninitialized or partially initialized member while the first thread is still creating it. The results can be unexpected,
potentially even causing the application to crash.
Bug_Explanation: The code contains the bug of using double-checked locking for the lazy initialization of an object, which is not reliable in a platform-independent manner for mutable instances.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug() method that creates two threads that attempt to access the getInstance() method simultaneously. Since double-checked locking is used in the getInstance() method, this can lead to unexpected results and trigger the bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results show that the test passed successfully without any exceptions. This indicates that the double-checked locking in the Java code did not cause any issues in this particular test run, so the described bug was not triggered.
